title: Update on Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme
subtitle:
PMNDP is presently implemented in all 36 States/UTs covering 751 districts, including 44 linked districts through 1,856 haemodialysis centres equipped with 13,535 haemodialysis machines
Union Health Ministry undertakes regular review of the Programme; non-operational dialysis centres, if any, are brought to the notice of the concerned State/UT for taking corrective action
body_text:
‘Public Health’ and ‘Hospitals’ are state subjects. However, the Government of India provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs under the National Health Mission (NHM) for strengthening healthcare infrastructure, including dialysis services.
Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP) was launched to improve access to haemodialysis services by establishing dialysis centres in District Hospitals and other health facilities across the country and providing free dialysis services to eligible patients. The Programme is presently implemented in all 36 States/UTs covering 751 districts (including 44 linked districts) through 1,856 haemodialysis centres equipped with 13,535 haemodialysis machines, as reported by the States/UTs as on 30.06.2026.
Dialysis centres under PMNDP were established based on proposals received from the States/UTs in their annual Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs), prepared on the basis of gap analysis. These proposals are considered in the National Programme Coordination Committee meetings and approvals are conveyed through the Record of Proceedings (RoPs). The State/UT-wise cumulative number of dialysis centres established under PMNDP, including those added during the last two years, is at Annexure-I.
The Ministry undertakes periodic monitoring of the Programme through the Common Review Mission (CRM) and visits by senior officers. During such reviews, non-operational dialysis centres, if any, are brought to the notice of the concerned State/UT for taking corrective action. The responsibility for timely operationalization of dialysis centres, deployment of adequately trained manpower including dialysis technicians, rests with the respective State/UT Governments and the implementing partner, wherever engaged.

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

enrichment.summary: The Union Health Ministry informed the Rajya Sabha that the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP) is now operational across all 36 States/UTs, covering 751 districts (including 44 linked districts) through 1,856 haemodialysis centres equipped with 13,535 haemodialysis machines, as of 30 June 2026. Minister of State Prataprao Jadhav stated that dialysis centres are established based on State/UT proposals under annual Programme Implementation Plans, approved via the National Programme Coordination Committee. The Ministry monitors the programme through Common Review Missions and officer visits, flagging non-operational centres to States/UTs for corrective action.
enrichment.context:
PMNDP was launched in 2016 under the National Health Mission to address the rising burden of chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease in India by providing free or subsidised haemodialysis services at district hospitals, especially benefiting poor and rural patients who previously had to travel long distances or bear high private costs for dialysis. Since 'Public Health' and 'Hospitals' are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule, the Centre's role is limited to technical and financial support via centrally sponsored schemes like NHM, while implementation, staffing, and operationalization remain State/UT responsibilities—a recurring governance tension highlighted in this reply.

The programme operates on a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model in many states, where private partners supply and maintain machines while the government provides space and consumables, aiming to expand access without heavy capital expenditure by states. The data shows uneven expansion, with states like Gujarat, Karnataka, and Maharashtra scaling up significantly, while others remain static, reflecting disparities in state capacity and priority. This periodic parliamentary reporting on PMNDP is also illustrative of how the Centre uses PIPs, National Programme Coordination Committee approvals, and Common Review Missions as tools for cooperative federalism in health governance.

prelims_questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP): 1. It is implemented under the National Health Mission. 2. 'Public Health' and 'Hospitals' fall under the State List of the Seventh Schedule. 3. The Programme is fully centrally funded and executed by the Union Government without State involvement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: PMNDP is implemented under NHM with Centre providing technical/financial support (statement 1 correct); Public Health and Hospitals are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule (statement 2 correct); but implementation and operationalization responsibility rests with States/UTs, not solely the Union Government (statement 3 incorrect).

prelims_questions.question: As per the latest government data (as on 30.06.2026), the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme is implemented across how many districts in India?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states PMNDP covers 751 districts (including 44 linked districts) across all 36 States/UTs as reported as on 30.06.2026.
